space-y-8 px-4"><span class="mb-2 font-medium text-muted-foreground text-sm">AI Foundations</span><div class="prose prose-lg"><h1 class="text-large mb-8">Hallucinations</h1><aside class="mdx-live-widget">
<p class="mdx-live-widget-label">Interactive explorer</p>
<p>This directory tree is interactive on the original page and cannot run inside an EPUB. Open it here: <a class="source-title" href="https://cursor.com/learn/hallucination-limitations#explore-the-directory" rel="external">https://cursor.com/learn/hallucination-limitations#explore-the-directory</a></p>
</aside>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Now that you understand how AI models work, let's talk about something that trips up many developers when they first start using AI tools: <strong>hallucination</strong>.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Hallucination is when an AI model confidently generates information that seems plausible but is actually incorrect. It's like when someone tries to bluff their way through a conversation about a topic they don't really know.</p>
<h2 class="text-medium mt-12 mb-4" id="why-do-models-hallucinate"><a aria-label="Copy link to why-do-models-hallucinate" class="group flex items-center no-underline hover:no-underline" data-heading-base-id="why-do-models-hallucinate" href="#why-do-models-hallucinate"><span data-heading-highlight-target="true">Why do models hallucinate?</span><span class="ml-2 text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"><div aria-hidden="true" class="relative size-3"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-copy absolute inset-0 size-3 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-100 scale-100" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect height="14" rx="2" ry="2" width="14" x="8" y="8"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-check absolute inset-0 size-3 text-green-600 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-0 scale-50" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></svg></div></span></a></h2>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Remember how we said AI models predict the next token based on patterns they've learned? Well, sometimes those patterns lead them astray.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Think of these models like extremely powerful text autocomplete. If you've typed "The weather today is..." your phone might suggest "sunny" or "cloudy" based on common patterns. AI models do the same thing, but with entire concepts and code blocks.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">When an AI model doesn't know something, it doesn't always say "I don't know." Instead, it generates what seems most likely based on patterns it has seen. For coding, this might mean:</p>
<ul class="my-6 prose-ul-markers" style="list-style-type:square;list-style-position:outside;padding-left:calc(4rem / 3);line-height:1.5">
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Inventing plausible-sounding API methods</strong> that don't actually exist</li>
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Mixing up syntax</strong> between different programming libraries or frameworks</li>
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Creating configuration options</strong> that seem reasonable but aren't real</li>
</ul>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">AI model providers take tons of text on the internet (and other proprietary data) to train models up until some date called the “knowledge cutoff”. This date is the latest knowledge models have. AI models may suggest incorrect solutions if you ask about libraries created after this date.</p>
<div aria-labelledby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-label" class="my-6 rounded-sm border p-4 border-border bg-card" role="group"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4"><p class="font-semibold text-foreground" id="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-label">Which is the best immediate response to a likely hallucinated API method?</p></div><div class="mt-3 space-y-2"><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-a-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="a"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Trust but implement and fix later.</div></div></label><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-b-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="b"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Verify in docs or your codebase; provide the error back to the model.</div></div></label><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-c-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="c"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Ask for three more alternatives and pick one.</div></div></label></div><div class="mt-3 flex items-center gap-2"><button class="inline-flex items-center rounded-sm border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm border-border bg-muted text-muted-foreground" disabled="" type="button">Check</button><button class="inline-flex items-center rounded-sm border border-border bg-card px-3 py-1.5 text-foreground text-sm" type="button">Reset</button></div></div>
<h2 class="text-medium mt-12 mb-4" id="hallucination-in-the-wild"><a aria-label="Copy link to hallucination-in-the-wild" class="group flex items-center no-underline hover:no-underline" data-heading-base-id="hallucination-in-the-wild" href="#hallucination-in-the-wild"><span data-heading-highlight-target="true">Hallucination in the wild</span><span class="ml-2 text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"><div aria-hidden="true" class="relative size-3"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-copy absolute inset-0 size-3 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-100 scale-100" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect height="14" rx="2" ry="2" width="14" x="8" y="8"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-check absolute inset-0 size-3 text-green-600 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-0 scale-50" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></svg></div></span></a></h2>

<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">As you work with AI models more, you’ll learn how to spot hallucinations.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">It’s worth being skeptical of the results you get back from the model, and verifying the suggestions it makes independently. One way to make this easier is by setting up your editor or application environment to give you feedback.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">For example, inside Cursor, an incorrect <code class="rounded-sm border border-border bg-card/80 p-1 font-mono text-xs">import</code> statement should show an error that the import does not exist, which can then be provided back to the AI model as feedback.</p>
<h2 class="text-medium mt-12 mb-4" id="other-model-limitations"><a aria-label="Copy link to other-model-limitations" class="group flex items-center no-underline hover:no-underline" data-heading-base-id="other-model-limitations" href="#other-model-limitations"><span data-heading-highlight-target="true">Other model limitations</span><span class="ml-2 text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"><div aria-hidden="true" class="relative size-3"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-copy absolute inset-0 size-3 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-100 scale-100" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect height="14" rx="2" ry="2" width="14" x="8" y="8"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-check absolute inset-0 size-3 text-green-600 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-0 scale-50" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></svg></div></span></a></h2>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Models can also confidently suggest the wrong answer.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">You might get a response that says “You’re absolutely right!” when in reality, you were <em>not</em> right. Further, some models struggle with things deterministic software is great at, like generating truly random numbers, or counting the number of occurrences of a character in a word.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">But even with hallucinations and limitations, AI models are still incredibly useful.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">The key to working effectively with AI is developing a verification mindset. Every suggestion is a starting point, not a final answer. This might sound like extra work, but it's actually making you a better developer by forcing you to understand what the code does rather than just copying it.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Throughout this course, we’ll suggest approaches you can take to improve the quality of the code generated and properly work with AI models.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Before we talk about how we can interact with the models, we need to understand more about how they think and how they are priced. Let’s dig into that more in our next lesson.<span class="inline-block size-2 bg-primary mx-auto ml-1"></span></p></div><div class="my-12 rounded-sm border border-border bg-card p-6 text-base"><h2 space-y-8 px-4"><span class="mb-2 font-medium text-muted-foreground text-sm">AI Foundations</span><div class="prose prose-lg"><h1 class="text-large mb-8">Hallucinations</h1>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Now that you understand how AI models work, let's talk about something that trips up many developers when they first start using AI tools: <strong>hallucination</strong>.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Hallucination is when an AI model confidently generates information that seems plausible but is actually incorrect. It's like when someone tries to bluff their way through a conversation about a topic they don't really know.</p>
<h2 class="text-medium mt-12 mb-4" id="why-do-models-hallucinate"><a aria-label="Copy link to why-do-models-hallucinate" class="group flex items-center no-underline hover:no-underline" data-heading-base-id="why-do-models-hallucinate" href="#why-do-models-hallucinate"><span data-heading-highlight-target="true">Why do models hallucinate?</span><span class="ml-2 text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"><div aria-hidden="true" class="relative size-3"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-copy absolute inset-0 size-3 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-100 scale-100" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect height="14" rx="2" ry="2" width="14" x="8" y="8"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-check absolute inset-0 size-3 text-green-600 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-0 scale-50" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></svg></div></span></a></h2>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Remember how we said AI models predict the next token based on patterns they've learned? Well, sometimes those patterns lead them astray.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Think of these models like extremely powerful text autocomplete. If you've typed "The weather today is..." your phone might suggest "sunny" or "cloudy" based on common patterns. AI models do the same thing, but with entire concepts and code blocks.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">When an AI model doesn't know something, it doesn't always say "I don't know." Instead, it generates what seems most likely based on patterns it has seen. For coding, this might mean:</p>
<ul class="my-6 prose-ul-markers" style="list-style-type:square;list-style-position:outside;padding-left:calc(4rem / 3);line-height:1.5">
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Inventing plausible-sounding API methods</strong> that don't actually exist</li>
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Mixing up syntax</strong> between different programming libraries or frameworks</li>
<li style="padding-inline-start:4px;margin:0 0 0.5rem 0;font-size:15px"><strong>Creating configuration options</strong> that seem reasonable but aren't real</li>
</ul>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">AI model providers take tons of text on the internet (and other proprietary data) to train models up until some date called the “knowledge cutoff”. This date is the latest knowledge models have. AI models may suggest incorrect solutions if you ask about libraries created after this date.</p>
<div aria-labelledby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-label" class="my-6 rounded-sm border p-4 border-border bg-card" role="group"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4"><p class="font-semibold text-foreground" id="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-label">Which is the best immediate response to a likely hallucinated API method?</p></div><div class="mt-3 space-y-2"><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-a-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="a"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Trust but implement and fix later.</div></div></label><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-b-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="b"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Verify in docs or your codebase; provide the error back to the model.</div></div></label><label class="flex w-full cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-sm border border-transparent px-3 py-2 transition-colors"><input aria-describedby="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-c-exp" class="mt-1 h-4 w-4 accent-primary" name="_R_4taqnpfiupiivb_-choices" type="radio" value="c"/><div class="flex-1"><div class="text-foreground text-sm">Ask for three more alternatives and pick one.</div></div></label></div><div class="mt-3 flex items-center gap-2"><button class="inline-flex items-center rounded-sm border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm border-border bg-muted text-muted-foreground" disabled="" type="button">Check</button><button class="inline-flex items-center rounded-sm border border-border bg-card px-3 py-1.5 text-foreground text-sm" type="button">Reset</button></div></div>

<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">As you work with AI models more, you’ll learn how to spot hallucinations.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">It’s worth being skeptical of the results you get back from the model, and verifying the suggestions it makes independently. One way to make this easier is by setting up your editor or application environment to give you feedback.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">For example, inside Cursor, an incorrect <code class="rounded-sm border border-border bg-card/80 p-1 font-mono text-xs">import</code> statement should show an error that the import does not exist, which can then be provided back to the AI model as feedback.</p>
<h2 class="text-medium mt-12 mb-4" id="other-model-limitations"><a aria-label="Copy link to other-model-limitations" class="group flex items-center no-underline hover:no-underline" data-heading-base-id="other-model-limitations" href="#other-model-limitations"><span data-heading-highlight-target="true">Other model limitations</span><span class="ml-2 text-muted-foreground opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"><div aria-hidden="true" class="relative size-3"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-copy absolute inset-0 size-3 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-100 scale-100" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect height="14" rx="2" ry="2" width="14" x="8" y="8"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg><svg aria-hidden="true" class="lucide lucide-check absolute inset-0 size-3 text-green-600 transition-all duration-200 ease-in-out opacity-0 scale-50" fill="none" height="24" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 24 24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></svg></div></span></a></h2>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Models can also confidently suggest the wrong answer.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">You might get a response that says “You’re absolutely right!” when in reality, you were <em>not</em> right. Further, some models struggle with things deterministic software is great at, like generating truly random numbers, or counting the number of occurrences of a character in a word.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">But even with hallucinations and limitations, AI models are still incredibly useful.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">The key to working effectively with AI is developing a verification mindset. Every suggestion is a starting point, not a final answer. This might sound like extra work, but it's actually making you a better developer by forcing you to understand what the code does rather than just copying it.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Throughout this course, we’ll suggest approaches you can take to improve the quality of the code generated and properly work with AI models.</p>
<p class="text-base mb-4 leading-relaxed!">Before we talk about how we can interact with the models, we need to understand more about how they think and how they are priced. Let’s dig into that more in our next lesson.<span class="inline-block size-2 bg-primary mx-auto ml-1"></span></p></div><div class="my-12 rounded-sm border border-border bg-card p-6 text-base"><h2 class="mb-4 text-base">You've completed this chapter</h2><div class="mt-4"><a class="inline-flex items-center font-medium text-primary transition-colors hover:text-primary/80" href="/learn/tokens-pricing">Keep learning<svg class="ml-1 h-4 w-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewbox="0 0 24 24"><title>Arrow pointing right</title><path d="M9 5l7 7-7 7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2"></path></svg></a></div></div></div></div></div></main></div></div><!--$--><!--/$--></div><!--$--><!--/$--></div></body></html>
